checks_that_could_have_failed: Three measurements, each with a control. (1) Faithfulness of the plotted values: pixel positions of all six stated-sd discs and all six doubled-noise rings were converted through each panel's own tick rows and compared with the record's tables; worst disagreement 0.004 (ITER direction 1, 0.896 measured against 0.898 tabulated), which is the pixel quantisation of the marker centre, and the band edges render at 0.744-1.307 against a stated 0.7447-1.3017. (2) The 99% circle: its radius measures 3.04-3.05 stated sd in all three renders (221.5 px at 72.9 px/unit on ITER, 213 px at 70.0 on MAST, 215 px at 70.7 on Solov'ev) and its centre lands on the zero crosshair to within 0.5 px, against the analytic sqrt(chi2.ppf(0.99,2)) = 3.0349 -- so the drawn interval is the interval the caption claims. (3) Label collision: the gap measure was shown to fire by dragging one text row 10 px into another in a copy of image-0, which moved the measured inter-band gap from 13 px to 3 px; an earlier version of the same check merged overlapping text into one oversized component and silently dropped it, reporting a clean result it could not have supported, so the band-gap form was used instead. A first attempt at the collision control also failed to fire because it moved a row in the wrong direction; that too is recorded rather than hidden. Nothing in the pixels contradicted the record: every ratio lies inside the band as the fragment states, and every control ratio lies outside it.

findings.disposition: folded: redraw the three figures with the population at full opacity (#929292, 3.1:1) and re-render; no other change to the plot is needed
findings.summary: The 256-point population is drawn as #929292 (full_study.py:372) at alpha 0.55 (line 385, composite of 146*0.55 + 255*0.45), so every dot renders at rgb(195,195,195), a contrast of 1.76:1 on white. Measured on all three rendered PNGs: the modal non-white luminance in each left panel is 195, with 1019-1067 pixels at exactly that value. That is below the 3:1 the project's plot style sets for a population grey (#929292 would reach 3.1:1 at full opacity) and lighter than the #B0B0B0 at 2.0:1 the lead rejected as too light. At reading size the 256 points merge into a pale field and the cloud's own extremes are harder to pick out than its density warrants; the marks are visible, so this does not hold the node. A correction to the record at head f0cd75cbf, which listed the grey marks at rgb(146,146,146) and 3.1:1: that value is the full-opacity dotted crosshair at lines 398-399, not the dots.

findings.disposition: folded: set the ratio panel's floor near the band (or draw the band on its own inset panel) so the distances to both edges are readable, in the same redraw as finding 1
findings.summary: The right panel's limits are set as set_ylim(0.0, upper * 1.15) with upper taken from the largest value drawn, so the axis floor is zero and the ceiling is driven by the twice-stated-sd control near 4: measured ceilings are 5.24 on ITER, 5.45 on MAST and 4.83 on Solov'ev. The acceptance band 0.7447 to 1.3017 therefore occupies 10.9, 10.5 and 12.0 per cent of the panel height (55, 53 and 59 px of 504, 504 and 493 px), while the markers themselves are 13-14 px across, a quarter of the band's height. The ITER direction-1 ratio of 0.898 sits 0.151 above the lower edge -- 27 per cent of the band -- yet only about one marker radius (8 px) clear of it, so a comfortable pass reads as marginal and a genuine near-threshold failure would be difficult to tell from a pass. How far inside each direction sits, which the record reports (0.898 to 1.259), cannot be read off the panel. This finding was recorded for these same figures at head f0cd75cbf and persists unchanged at this head, because the figures have not been redrawn; the plotted values, the mark colours and the inside/outside verdict are all correct.

findings.disposition: folded: give the two panels a fixed equal-aspect box (shared limits across the three states) in the same redraw as finding 1
findings.summary: left.set_aspect("equal") re-fits and centres the left axes box, so in the Solov'ev render that panel occupies rows 120-613 (493 px) against rows 115-619 (504 px) in the ITER and MAST renders, while the right panel stays 504 px in all three. Within the Solov'ev image the left panel's x-axis baseline therefore sits 5 px above the right panel's, and the figure's leftmost ink begins at x=51 against x=66 on ITER and x=78 on MAST. A reader comparing the three figures in sequence sees left panels of two different scales whose horizontal position shifts by up to 27 px, and inside the Solov'ev figure two panels whose baselines do not line up. No label is clipped and nothing is unreadable, which is why this does not hold the node; a shared x/y limit or a fixed gridspec width would align the panels without changing the aspect rule that the circle requires.

item_verdicts.contrast: pass for every text element, measured on the rendered pixels: legend and axis-label glyph cores are rgb(11,11,11) at 19.7:1 on white and tick labels rgb(80,80,80) at 8.1:1, both clearing WCAG AA. The data marks do not clear 3:1 -- the population grey renders at rgb(195,195,195), 1.76:1 -- which is recorded as finding 1 rather than as a text-contrast failure, because the rubric's contrast item is about text and the text here is unambiguous.
item_verdicts.data_ink: pass on all three: the ink is the data. The left panel carries 256 grey points, one dashed circle of radius 3.04 stated sd and a dotted zero crosshair; the right panel carries two filled blue discs, two hollow rings, one dotted unity line and the acceptance band. No gridlines and no top or right spines: the only long ink columns in each image are the two left spines (x=154/166/139 and x=837) and the only long ink rows are the two bottom spines.
item_verdicts.decoration: pass on all three: pure white covers 94.4, 94.4 and 94.2 per cent of the canvas; there is no gradient, no texture and no themed background. The single fill is the right panel acceptance band, whose extent is the measured interval -- 0.7447 to 1.3017 by construction, rendered as 0.744-1.307, 0.744-1.306 and 0.745-1.302 by pixel measurement -- and the caption names it, so its area carries information rather than decoration.
item_verdicts.label_collision: pass on all three, checked at native resolution: the outer two pixel rows and columns of every image are pure white, so nothing is clipped at the canvas edge; ink margins are 17 px top, 41/41/47 px bottom, 66/78/51 px left and 15 px right; the smallest vertical gap between adjacent text bands is 6 px in the ITER and MAST figures and 5 px in the Solov'ev figure; the two legend columns are 47 px apart and the two legend rows 13 px apart. The measure was shown to be sensitive: dragging the second legend row 10 px up in a copy of image-0 reduced the inter-band gap from 13 px to 3 px.
item_verdicts.legibility: pass on all three, with a recorded caveat (finding 1): 1399x720 canvas, 16 pt axis labels naming quantity and unit ("principal 1 [stated sd]", "principal 2 [stated sd]", "realised / stated variance"), 14 pt tick and legend text, two panels that read at a glance. The dashed 99% circle, the dotted zero crosshair, the filled blue discs and the hollow grey rings separate by shape as well as colour. The caveat: the 256-point population renders at rgb(195,195,195), 1.76:1 on white, so the cloud is legible at native resolution but its centre merges into a pale field at reading size; the individual extremes and the circle remain visible, which is why this is non-blocking.
item_verdicts.table_form: pass on all three: the left panel is a two-dimensional scatter against a reference contour, a spatial relationship no table carries; the right panel puts four numbers against a shaded interval so that inside and outside are visible without arithmetic. The same six ratios also appear in the record's tables, but the two panels add the scatter and the band comparison, neither of which is a table.

notes: Read-only figure review of the three rendered PNGs named in the review brief. No SVG, no preview image and no image other than those three was opened, rendered or git-shown, and no file was edited, redrawn, relabelled, moved or reformatted.
